# Complete the customer billing-schedule migration

Finish the service-to-customer migration for recurring billing. Creating a customer must create a monthly billing schedule only when that customer has an offering. When an existing customer gains or changes an `offeringId`, replace any previous billing schedule with a customer-level schedule; an already-missing old schedule is not an error. Preserve the authenticated subject and business ID in the scheduler configuration.

Billing jobs receive `businessID` on the scheduler record and `customerId` in `scheduleParameters`. Resolve the customer and its offering, derive the offering billing-cycle time range, call the existing usage-total invoice path with that exact customer and range, and persist a billing record containing the returned invoice ID. Report processing failures through the existing audit channel instead of leaving the queue job with a partially stored billing record.

Route billing scheduler emissions to `scheduler_billing_queue` with the `billingReport` consumer name. All non-billing measurements must continue to use the normal scheduler queue and their dimension consumer. Finally, a usage read for a customer without an offering should return an empty result rather than fail.

Verify with:

    cd /app && npm run build && npm run test:ci -- --runInBand
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the current state of this migration.

The migration is complete. `npm run build` and `npm run test:ci -- --runInBand` both pass (43 suites / 70 tests).

## Changes

**Customer-level billing schedules** — `src/customer/customer.service.ts`
- `create` now only schedules billing when the new customer actually has an `offeringId`; the scheduling logic moved into a private `createBillingSchedule` helper that keeps `subject` and `businessID` on the scheduler config (`customer.service.ts:37`, `customer.service.ts:51`).
- `update` detects a gained/changed `offeringId` and calls `replaceBillingSchedule`, which removes the previous billing-queue schedule (tolerating `NotFoundException`) before creating the customer-level one (`customer.service.ts:76`, `customer.service.ts:247`).
- The authenticated subject is threaded through: the controller now forwards `sub` (`customer.controller.ts:145`), and `update` accepts it explicitly or from the payload of internal callers.

**Billing job** — `src/billing/billing.service.ts`
- Reads `businessID` off the scheduler record (falling back to the parameters) and `customerId` from `scheduleParameters`, resolves the customer plus its offering via `CustomerService`, derives the range with `Billing.billingCycleToTimeRange`, and calls `invoicesService.generateInvoiceForUsageTotal` with that exact customer/range, persisting a `Billing` record with the returned `invoiceId`.
- Customers without an offering are a no-op log; any processing failure is reported via `AuditService.publishEvent({ topic: AuditScope.ERROR, ... })` so the job never leaves a partially stored billing record.
- `ServicesService` is no longer a dependency; `billing.module.ts` and `billing.service.spec.ts` now wire the customer module instead.

**Scheduler emissions** — `src/scheduler/scheduler.service.ts:227`
- `emitOne` routes `schedulerType.billing` to `scheduler_billing_queue` under the `billingReport` consumer; every other measurement still goes to `scheduler_queue` with its `dimensionType` consumer.

**Usage reads** — `src/usage/usage.service.ts:58`
- A customer without an offering now logs and returns `[]` instead of throwing `ConflictException`, so callers (customer usage endpoint, usage-total invoices, dimension aggregation) degrade to an empty result.
